title: Signal bridge: demand-aware structured log stitcher with OTLP trace hooks and fanout throttling
creator: Ava Chen
description: Build a demand-aware ‘signal bridge’ component in the ingress path that stitches structured logs to traces via OTLP hooks, enforces schema contracts for tenant events, and performs smart fanout throttling to downstream aggregation backends (Loki + ELK). Goals: reduce end-to-end log->trace join latency for trace-linked requests, avoid tail-latency amplification from noisy tenants, and provide deterministic label extraction for Loki indexing while preserving lossless ordering guarantees for tenant-sensitive flows.
acceptance_criteria: OTLP trace hooks attach span_id and trace_id to enriched log envelopes for >=99.9% of traceable requests in integration tests
Per-tenant fastpath triggers when 95th-percentile ingest latency < 40ms at target throughput and falls back to buffered fanout when overloaded
Loki label extraction matches schema mapping in Confluence and produces <1% label parsing errors in production traffic
Backpressure and throttling controls prevent downstream queue growth > 3x baseline without dropping high-priority trace-linked logs
End-to-end system tests exercising lossless ordering for tenant-critical streams (replayable with synthetic sequence ids) pass in CI
implementation_notes: Introduce an ingress stage 'signal-bridge' that lives after protobuf->json normalization and before enrichment
Signal-bridge will subscribe to our internal OTLP consumer topic to resolve span context for delayed arrival orders (span may arrive after log) using a small LRU cache with TTL
Canonicalize correlation ids: accept x-corr, traceparent, and our legacy 'corr_id' and materialize to 'corr_id.canonical' label for Loki
Fastpath mode: route small structured events (<= 2KB, validated schema) through a low-latency path that bypasses full enrichment and uses a lightweight KV cache for common label sets
Buffered fanout: large or schema-invalid events are buffered to partitioned write queues with tenant-aware reordering and deterministic commit markers to preserve ordering on replay
Throttling policy: token-bucket per-tenant with global emergency pool; when breached, degrade by sampling non-trace-linked debug logs first
Metrics: add ingress.span_lookup_latency_seconds, ingress.fastpath_hit_ratio, ingress.throttle_events_total, and per-tenant backlog_gauge
Expose tracing hooks to the runtime sidecar so that service-side SDKs may annotate logs if span context is known at emission time (opt-in toggles)
Persist small span->log join metadata in RocksDB with compaction; TTL aligns to trace retention (30 min default)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: increased memory usage from span lookup cache. Mitigation: LRU with strict hard limit and metrics to trigger auto-scale of sidecar memory pool
Risk: label explosion in Loki from heterogeneous schemas. Mitigation: enforce a curated label whitelist per-tenant and drop-to-secondary-index for unknown keys
Risk: ordering regressions during failover. Mitigation: include commit markers and sequence checkpoints in buffered fanout and cross-check during consumer replay
Risk: delayed spans causing false negatives for trace-linked logs. Mitigation: extend span lookup window and attempt re-join during consumer pass with metrics on re-join rate
testing_plan: Unit: schema validator fuzz tests, correlation id canonicalizer property tests
Integration: end-to-end with OTLP bridge, synthetic trace/log pairs covering out-of-order arrival and partial failures
Load: k6 + custom harness to simulate 100k events/s with tenant skew (10 tenants producing 90% of traffic) and assert 95th latency SLA
Chaos: kill downstream Loki/ELK writers to validate buffered fanout and replay correctness
Observability: dashboard panels for fastpath ratio, span-join latency, per-tenant throttle rate; alert if fastpath_hit_ratio < 0.6 under nominal load
rollout_and_migration: Deploy to staging without fastpath enabled for 48h, validate metrics and correctness against replayed logs
Canary: enable fastpath for 5% of tenant traffic (low-volume tenants) and observe ingress metrics for 24h
Gradual ramp: 5->25->50->100% with monitoring gates at each step and automated rollback on SLO breaches
Migration: run a dual-write mode where legacy enrichers continue to receive events while consumers switch to new labels; provide a 'compat' label mapper for 30 days
notes_and_links: Incident reference: INC-2024-11-08-loki-backpressure (lessons learned applied to throttling policy)
